findings.finding: lock generation/sequencer evidence must be carried to and validated by the recipient of the protected operation; lock possession alone is insufficient against delayed/stale operations
findings.architecture_implication: B3/provider boundary generation revalidation is structurally justified

findings.source: Amazon Builders Library - Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
findings.finding: timeout can leave outcome indeterminate; stable caller request identity, atomic idempotency recording, and reconciliation are required to avoid duplicate side effects
findings.architecture_implication: OUTCOME_UNKNOWN plus stable provider request identity/reconciliation is preferable to blind retry

findings.source: Stripe API idempotent requests and error handling
findings.finding: same idempotency key is safe only for semantically identical retries; ambiguous connection/API outcomes must not be guessed
findings.architecture_implication: provider contract must bind key to semantic request fingerprint and preserve indeterminate outcomes

go_out_of_box_experiment.method: Use the exact self-hosted PR250 merge checkout as the authority boundary and let the frontend probe resolve its bound grammar path without copying sibling artifacts or fallback inference.
go_out_of_box_experiment.observation: The exact checkout passed Gate/effect/semantic-contract tests but failed immediately because the bound WP03 grammar file did not exist in the branch merge graph.
go_out_of_box_experiment.rollback: No product mutation was made; PR250 received an adjudication comment only.
